action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: axcheck.sh Module.Name [Module.Name ...]   (run after lake build of those modules)
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref
F=$SP/axcheck_$$.lean
{
  echo "import Lean"
  for m in "$@"; do echo "import $m"; done
  echo 'open Lean Elab Command in'
  echo '#eval show Lean.Core.CoreM Unit from do'
  echo '  let env ← getEnv'
  printf '  for modName in [%s] do\n' "$(printf '`%s, ' "$@" | sed 's/, $//')"
  cat <<'L'
    let some mod := env.getModuleIdx? modName | throwError "no module"
    let mut all := 0
    let mut thms := 0
    let mut bad : Array (Name × Array Name) := #[]
    for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
      if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some mod then
        all := all + 1
        if let .thmInfo _ := ci then thms := thms + 1
        let axs ← collectAxioms n
        let extra := axs.filter fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound
        if !extra.isEmpty then bad := bad.push (n, extra)
    IO.println s!"{modName}: constants {all}, theorems {thms}"
    IO.println s!"outside propext, Quot.sound: {bad}"
L
} > $F
cd /Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern/formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean $F
rm -f $F

3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).

Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.

Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.

Exclusions: instrumented checked variants; duplicate _pre statements; references to draft reports; concurrency beyond the stat boundary; syntax.
Rules: zero sorry; #print axioms at most {propext, Quot.sound} on every constant (checked by script); no noncomputable; lake build without warnings; nothing invented - a clause that cannot be formalized as written is reported, not interpreted; no statement weakened relative to its clause; adversarial review rounds, every finding re-checked by a refuter.

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

"""Build table-final.md and citation-index.md from the scripted extraction.

Inputs (this directory): decls_wt.json, decls_head.json, decls_base.json (extract.py on the working tree,
HEAD and a14dda0~1), index_wt.json (index.py), rows_final.py. Run: python3 -I gen_final.py OUT_DIR
"""
import json, re, sys, runpy, collections, os

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = sys.argv[1]
J = lambda p: json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, p)))
rows = runpy.run_path(os.path.join(HERE, 'rows_final.py'))
ROWS, BRIEF = rows['ROWS'], rows['BRIEF']

def short(n):
    return n.replace('Ern.MemoryModel.', '').replace('Ern.Lib.', 'Lib.').replace('Ern.Corpus.', 'Corpus.')

def table(p):
    return {(short(r['name']), r['kind']): r for r in J(p)
            if r['kind'] != 'example' and not r['name'].endswith(')')}
base, head, wt = table('decls_base.json'), table('decls_head.json'), table('decls_wt.json')
names = lambda t: {n for n, _ in t}
added_c = names(head) - names(base)
added_w = names(wt) - names(head)
removed = names(base) - names(wt)
stmt = {n for (n, k) in set(base) & set(head) if base[(n, k)].get('sig') != head[(n, k)].get('sig')}
stmt |= {n for (n, k) in set(head) & set(wt) if head[(n, k)].get('sig') != wt[(n, k)].get('sig')}
docd = {n for (n, k) in set(base) & set(wt) if base[(n, k)]['doc'] != wt[(n, k)]['doc']} - stmt

# Renames (reports/fix1-pool.md HP-1), checked: same statement modulo the name.
RENAMED = {
    'Lib.HandlePool.freeGuarantee_of': 'Lib.HandlePool.freeGuaranteeSamePool_of',
    'Lib.HandlePool.pool_inv_preserved': 'Lib.HandlePool.pool_inv_preserved_same_pool',
    'Lib.HandlePool.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc': 'Lib.HandlePool.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool',
    'Lib.HandlePool.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive': 'Lib.HandlePool.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool',
}
assert set(RENAMED) == removed, (removed, set(RENAMED))
def last(n): return n.split('.')[-1]
for o, n in RENAMED.items():
    so = base[(o, 'theorem')]['sig'].replace(last(o), '@'); sn = wt[(n, 'theorem')]['sig'].replace(last(n), '@')
    so = so.replace('FreeGuarantee ', 'FreeGuaranteeSamePool ').replace('PoolInv ', 'PoolInvSamePool ')
    assert so == sn, (o, so, sn)
# Redefinitions (body changed, name kept): bodies.py reports FreeGuarantee; PoolInv changes through it.
REDEF = {'Lib.HandlePool.FreeGuarantee': 'redefined: literal D.4 (3); the former body is `FreeGuaranteeSamePool`',
         'Lib.HandlePool.PoolInv': 'meaning changed: now uses the literal `FreeGuarantee`; the former meaning is `PoolInvSamePool`'}

docd -= set(REDEF)

def mark(n):
    m = ''
    if n in added_c: m += '†'
    if n in added_w: m += '‡'
    if n in stmt or n in REDEF: m += 'Δ'
    if n in docd: m += 'δ'
    return m

allnames = names(wt)
kinds = {}
for (n, k) in wt: kinds.setdefault(n, k)
idx = J('index_wt.json')['index']
nocite = J('index_wt.json')['nocite']
old_idx = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, '../review2/coverage/index.json')))

def keylist(keys):
    out = []
    for k in keys:
        out.append(k)
        if re.fullmatch(r'\d+', k): out.append(k + '~')
    return out

def old_keys(keys):
    out = []
    for k in keys:
        m = re.fullmatch(r'(\d+)(?:\.(\d+)| (¶\d+))?', k)
        a, i, p = m.groups()
        out.append(str((int(a), int(i) if i else (p if p else None))))
        if not i and not p: out.append(str((int(a), 'range')))
    return out

PRI = {'structure': 0, 'inductive': 0, 'class': 0, 'def': 1, 'abbrev': 1, 'field': 2, 'theorem': 3}
CAP = 8
missing = []

def fmt(n, cites=True):
    s = f'`{n}`{mark(n)}'
    if not cites: s += '°'
    return s

def decl_cell(keys, prio):
    model, corpus = [], set()
    for k in keylist(keys):
        for d in idx.get(k, []):
            if d['kind'] == 'instance' or d['name'].endswith(')'): continue
            if d['mod'].startswith('Corpus'): corpus.add(d['name']); continue
            if d['name'] not in model: model.append(d['name'])
    citing = set(model)
    shown = []
    for p in prio:
        if p not in allnames: missing.append(p); continue
        if p not in shown: shown.append(p)
    rest = sorted((n for n in model if n not in shown),
                  key=lambda n: (0 if mark(n) else 1, PRI.get(kinds.get(n), 4), n))
    for n in rest:
        if len(shown) >= CAP: break
        shown.append(n)
    more = len(citing - set(shown))
    cell = ', '.join(fmt(n, n in citing) for n in shown)
    if more: cell += f' (+{more} more citing)'
    olds = set()
    for k in old_keys(keys):

wave's `transfer_preserves` is false as stated for these definitions.

**SP-A2 §71.2 vs §36 [policy: record].** §71.2 "permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid
`writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata"; §36 "Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant
the right to create ... exclusive authority over the administered storage". `AllocStatic.providerRight`
follows §71.2 literally: `alloc` can create a root `Modify` authority with only an `Observe` right on a
`SharedMutable` provider. Example: provider leaf `SharedMutable`, an `Observe` derivative held by the
frame and no `Modify` on it: §71.2 accepts, §36 forbids.

# Readings — arena (`formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Arena.lean`, spec v0 Part XIV)

Each entry gives the clause, a quote, the reading used, the alternative, and a program whose verdict
changes. Machine-checked witnesses are in the `Witness` namespace of the module and are decided by
`decide`.

## A-R766. §76.6 omitted from `NewArenaBase` pending arbitration (supersedes reports/arena.md:129-130)

**Clause.** §76.6, a precondition of O17 `newArena`: "Dependency, holder, storage, and
administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected
arena invariants."

**Correction of the earlier record.** reports/arena.md:129-130 said "§76.6: not a precondition (no
checkable content beyond the invariants; WF3 is not decidable); `newArena_clause6` proves it
redundant under `KInv`." Both reasons are wrong:
- Decidability is no reason to omit the clause. `Guarded` (Access/Basic.lean, §58) takes any
  `Prop`, and every predicate the clause lists is defined (`WF3` §49, `I1` §50, `AnchorOrder` and
  `AnchorOrderHeld` §44, `ArenaInv` §55).
- `newArena_clause6` shows the clause is redundant only on `KInv` states. The §63 cycle
  (`Access.reachable_kinv_false`) makes non-`KInv` states library-reachable, and on those the clause
  changes the verdict (examples below).

**Status.** The model implements neither reading. `NewArenaBase`, `NewArenaPre`, `NewArenaStep`,
`LStep` and `LStepNG` are unchanged. Both readings are defined as `Prop`s and compared with the model.

**Reading (G), global: `NewArena766Global L`.** The kernel state satisfies `WF3 ∧ I1 ∧ AnchorOrder ∧
AnchorOrderHeld`, and every live entry of the registry satisfies `ArenaInv`.

**Reading (L), local: `NewArena766Local s st i`.** Only the relations of the new arena count:
- the clauses of `WF3` (§49.2, §49.3, §49.7), `AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` whose bound place
  is the storage `st` or the arena value (the place holding `i`) (`PlaceRel766`);
- the clauses of `WF3` (§49.4, §49.5, §49.6, §49.8) and `I1` whose bound authority is `internal`
  (`AuthRel766`);
- `ArenaInv` of the new entry `⟨st, i, footprint st, []⟩`.

§49.1 (the frame stack) concerns no relation of the arena and is not part of (L). Restricting (L)
to these objects is itself part of the reading submitted for arbitration. For example, it excludes
the parts of the storage and I3, which §76.6 does not list.

A third, mixed reading is possible: kernel predicates over the whole state, but `ArenaInv` of the
new entry only. On both examples below it gives the verdict of (G), since `WF3` fails there.

**Departure or arrival state.** §76 leaves this open, so both are defined.
- For departure: §76.6 is listed among the preconditions and does not say "in the resulting state".
  §58 evaluates changes in the resulting state only "when a rule explicitly so provides", as §63.6,
  §63.7, §77.3 and §77.6 do.
- For arrival: "the expected arena invariants" of the new arena concern an entry that exists only
  after registration.
- The kernel component is the same in both states (Part XIV preamble, §76 `ok` effect,
  `newArena_kernel`).
- (G) is evaluated as `NewArena766Global L` (departure) or `NewArena766Global (newArenaEff L st i)`
  (arrival). The two are equivalent whenever `NewArenaBase` holds (`newArena766Global_arrival_iff`),
  so this choice changes no verdict.
- (L) reads only the kernel and the new entry, so its departure and arrival forms coincide.

**Relations proved.**
- `newArena766Local_of_global`: (G) together with `NewArenaBase` implies (L).
- `newArena766Local_of_kinv`: `KInv` together with `NewArenaBase` implies (L).
- `newArena766Global_of_kinv`: `KInv`, `LInv` and `NewArenaBase` imply (G) on the departure and the
  arrival state. `LInv` provides the registry conjunct, which is not a kernel predicate.
- These generalize `newArena_clause6`, which is unchanged except for its docstring. The gap between
  the model and §76.6 therefore lies only on non-`KInv` states, and for (G) also on states that
  violate `LInv`.

**Programs whose verdict changes.** Both start from `Examples.st` under `K0`: static leaf 0 `Init`,
leaves 1 and 2 `Uninit`, and root authorities 0, 1 and 2 held by frame 0.

1. `Witness.newArena766_global_fails_local_holds`: the model accepts, (G) rejects, (L) accepts.
   - Program: `alloc` place 3 (owned by 0); `alloc` 4 (owned by 3); `alloc` 5 (owned by 3);
     `derive(4,[4],Modify)` gives 6; `store(6,5)`; `newArena(4,6)`; `transfer(0,4)` closes the cycle
     3 ↔ 4; `derive(1,[1],Modify)` gives 7; `store(7,2)`; `newArena(1,7)`.
   - The model accepts the last step.
   - (G) rejects it. `WF3` fails because §49.8 is violated: the active authority 6 is held by the
     unusable place 5. The live entry `tE` also violates `ArenaInv`, since its storage 4 is unusable.
   - (L) accepts it: storage 1, arena value 2 and `internal` 7 are untouched by the cycle.
2. `Witness.newArena766_local_fails`: the model accepts, (G) and (L) both reject.
   - Program: `alloc` 3 (owned by 0); `alloc` 4 (owned by 3); `alloc` 5 (owned by 3);
     `derive(1,[1],Modify)` gives 6; `store(6,5)`; `derive(5,[5],Modify)` gives 7, held by frame 0;
     `transfer(0,4)`; `newArena(1,6)`.
   - The model accepts the last step. `internal` 6 is still exercisable through 7 (§43), and the new
     entry satisfies `ArenaInv`, because §55 does not require the arena value to be usable.
   - `internal` is held by the unusable place 5, so §49.8 fails at `internal`. Both (G) and (L)
     reject. The registry is empty, so (G) fails through its kernel part alone.
# Readings — handlepool (`formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean`, non-normative library instance)

Contract: "HandlePool v0.4 annex" (Annex D, items D.1–D.4, of `ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`),
corrected by spec v0 §36 (MetaRight = exercisable `Modify` on the pool value, no `writeShared` branch)
and §56 (guard over all registries of live administrations), and by brief obligation 5.
Spec v0 §75 / Part XIV preamble: the HandlePool contract "belong[s] to [its] library abstraction[s] and
[is] not defined here" (mapping P0). Every definition below that goes beyond §36/§37/§38/§46/§47/§56/
§58/§89 encodes the non-normative contract.

Each entry: clause, quote, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict changes.
Machine-checked witnesses are in the `Witness` namespace of the module (decided by `decide`).

## A. Readings that can change an accepted program (need arbitration)

**H-R1 (mapping P1). Which subplaces are slots.** D.1: "Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à
deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage`"; `newPool(storage, internal)` takes no slot description.
Used (draft): the direct children of `storage`, in index order (`kids`), each free, generation 0
(`newPoolEff`). Alternatives: the leaves of `storage`; a slot list passed to `newPool`.
Example: storage `S = {a: {x, y}, b}`: children give slots `a, b` (third `allocSlot` → `fail`);
leaves give `x, y, b` (third `allocSlot` → `ok`). A storage that is a leaf has no slot: every
`allocSlot` gives `fail`.

**H-R2 (mapping P2). `freeSlot` of a free slot whose identity and generation match.** D.3: "un slot
déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité" (excludes `ok`, does not say which
outcome). Used: `fail` (same handle validation `HandleOK` as `resolve`, D.2 "slot … libre ⇒ `fail`").
Alternative: `reject`. Example: fresh pool, `freeSlot(⟨id, 0, 0⟩)` on free slot 0: `fail` (used) vs
`reject`. Theorem `pool_freeSlot_stale_other_free_fails`.

**H-R3 (mapping P3). `resolve`/`resolveMany`/`freeSlot`: right before handle validity.** D.2 orders
handle validation "avant toute création d'autorité", not against the right; §58 "according to the
operation's contract". Used (draft): `reject` without the right (`ResolveRight` = `DerivePre` of the
companion; `AdminRight` for `freeSlot`), then `fail` for an invalid handle. Alternative (§77
analogy): handle `fail` first. Example: with an active `Modify` companion, `resolve(stale h, Modify)`:
`reject` (used) vs `fail`.

**H-R4. Missing pool index.** D.2/D.3 do not say what `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `allocSlot`, `freeSlot`
do on a registry index that names no pool. Used (draft): `reject`. Alternative: `fail`.

**H-R5 (mapping P4). Scope of "excluding `internal` and its ancestors" in `freeSlot`.** D.3: "aucune
autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; brief: "freeSlot ends the entry
content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors". Used
(`ContentEndPre`, x exempt iff `x = internal ∨ x ∈ ancs internal`):
- entry: no active authority covers a leaf of the slot place unless exempt (D.3 clause, which also
  subsumes §69.2 on the entry leaves);
- §69.2 on storage that dies with the content (`DyingAccessOK`): **unchanged**, no exemption;
- §69.3 (`ContentAnchorOK`): the exemption removes only the "its root" part (`IsRootOf`) for exempt
  anchors; "held by `place`" and "would become inactive when an owned holder dies" are kept for every
  anchor (they are what keeps I3, §52; an exempt anchor that the effect deactivates would leave a
  usable place with an invalid anchor);
- §69.4 pins: unchanged;
- §69.1 is not a precondition: `freeSlot_modify_right` derives `Usable slot` and
  `HasRight Modify slot` from `AdminRight` + the entry clause on well-formed pools.
Alternatives: (a) exempt `internal`/ancestors in §69.2 also on dying storage; (b) exempt them from
§69.3 entirely. (a) changes no verdict if `internal` and its ancestors never cover storage that dies
with a slot (expected under §49.6 RootChain: one root per covered chain; not proved here). (b) drops
the checks that keep an exempt anchor active: if a usable place depended on `internal` while
`internal` were held within the slot or by a dying holder, the result would violate I3 (§52); whether
such a state also passes the entry clause and `AdminRight` is not settled here, so (b) is not proven
to change a verdict.

**H-R6. `allocSlot` destination right.** D.3 lists "destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active,
non `Init`". Used: also `HasRight Modify dst` (the handle is written into `dst`, an O10 write §67.1;
draft). Alternative: not checked. Example: a destination with only `Observe`: `reject` (used) vs `ok`.

**H-R7. `allocSlot` choice.** D.3: "`ok` choisit un slot libre". Used: relation over any free slot
(mapping R6/B26), not the lowest index. No outcome set is narrowed.

**H-R8. `newPool` obligations taken from `newArena`.** D.1: "Il reprend les autres obligations
applicables de `newArena`". Used: all of §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 (`Arena.NewArenaBase`), including "all
leaves of the value holding `internal` are `Init`" (draft). Alternative: drop §76.5 as inapplicable.
Example: a pool value with an `Uninit` metadata leaf: `reject` (used) vs `ok`.

**H-R9 (mapping P10). `resolveMany Observe` with an invalid handle.** D.2 states the atomic `fail`
only in the `Modify` sentence. Used: atomic `fail` in both modes (`BatchOK`); distinctness only in
`Modify`. Alternative: no validation in `Observe`. Example: `resolveMany([stale h], Observe)`: `fail`
(used) vs `ok`.

**H-R10. Entry derivations rejected.** The kernel steps of a resolution are checked: if the entry
`derive` (resolve), the `split` (resolveMany Modify) or one of the `Observe` derives (resolveMany
Observe) is not accepted, the outcome is `reject` with no state (atomic). D.2: "Les deux sont soumises
aux règles ordinaires". Alternative: none found.

**H-R11. `unresolve`.** D.2: "libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la
compagne". Used: the entries active at the start of `unresolve`, in record order, then the companion;
`reject` if one release is not accepted or the companion is unknown (ghost lookup). The ghost record
is kept.

## B. Representation choices (no accepted program changes)

- Library state `PState = ⟨kern : S3, pools, nId, res⟩` outside `S3` (§38, §46); pool identity a
  counter `nId` (§9 ¶7 analogue); registry index `j` designates the pool of an operation.
- Ghost resolutions `Res` (pool, internal, companion, mode, entries tagged with slot and generation):
  auxiliary information creating no right (§38), read only by `unresolve` and the invariants.
- `AdminRight s pl := Active internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry` (reuses the arena's §36
  `MetaRight`: `HasRight Modify` on the place holding `internal`).
- §56 guard: `NewPoolPre.guard : Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal`; `others` (the
  other registries of live administrations, e.g. arenas and stacks) is a parameter of each `newPool`
  step, as in `Arena.NewArenaStep`.
- Outcomes: `Outcome3 PState`; `fail` and `reject` carry no state, so "state unchanged" is by
  construction (§58).
- `resolveMany Observe` = companion derive + successive `Observe` derives (`DerivesPre`,
  `derivesEff`); `Modify` = companion derive + `split` (mapping R5).
- `freeSlot` kernel effect = the O12 effect function `endUseEff` on the slot place (§69 effect), not an
  `EndUseStep`.
- Handles are not stored as values (no value layer in `S3`); `allocSlot` writes `dst` (`write3Eff`)
  and `slotHandle` gives the handle.

## C. Clauses not represented (no state content)

- D.3 "apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle" (Spec 4 / Spec 11): no sizes or types in `S3`
  (policy: omit and record). Mapping suggested a `HandleFits` parameter; not added (policy).
- D.1 "leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets": refinement, out of scope.
- D.4 generation overflow, encapsulation (Spec 9), persistent handle cycles: outside the abstract model.

# Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, all by `decide` on
library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. No verdict changes on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft].

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft
`case_grow`]: `reject` (`GrowStep.noBlock`). Alternative: `fail`, by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m
fails on a dead or foreign mark" (an identifier the stack does not record). Example
(`Ern.Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`, decided): after
`grow(0, 6, 1)` replaced block 6 by block 9 (`ds03.stacks` records the blocks `[⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩]`
only), `grow(0, 6, 1)` is `reject` here and `fail` under the alternative (the step reaches
`noBlock` and no other rule).

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard
(`Arena.NewArenaBase`: §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 "All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are
already `Init`", read for a stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)` (§56). Alternative: drop
§76.5 for a stack (DS-v1 does not take over `newArena`). Same choice as H-R8 for pools. Example
(`Witness.reading_newStack`, decided on the initial state of statics `wsu`): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owns
the storage leaf 1 and so holds its root authority 1 (§47); `newStack(1, 1)` is `reject` (only
§76.5 fails: every other field of `NewArenaBase` and the guard hold), `ok` under the alternative.

**DS-R10 `mark` requires no right [draft]** (was R6; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1 says nothing about
a right for `mark`. Reading: `ok` on an existing stack, `reject` on a missing one; `mark` changes
library metadata only and creates no right (§36 ¶2, §38). Alternative: §36 ¶1, metadata is modified
"to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts", so `mark` needs a right on the
stack value (`AdminRight`, or a valid `writeShared` over it, §68), else `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_mark`): in `d13` (a callee frame entered after the rewind), the callee has no
`AdminRight`, no `Observe` right on the stack value 0 and no valid `writeShared` over it through any
authority; `mark(0)` is `ok` (a mark appended), `reject` under the alternative.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

## Readings that change no accepted program (representation)

- **R1 State.** `DState = ⟨kern, stacks, fresh⟩`, separate from `S3` (§38, §46); a stack is its
  registry index, stacks are never removed; `fresh` is a global counter (§9 "a monotonically
  increasing counter is one possible representation"). The arena registry is not in `DState`: the
  guard reads it through the parameter `others` (§56), as `Arena.NewArenaPre` reads stacks through
  its `others`.
- **R2 Available cells** = positions `≥ top` of the ordered cells (`Stack.entry.available =
  cells.drop top`); `push` and `grow` take cells at the top only and `rewind` returns exactly
  `above`, so this is a set of leaves as in §46.
- **R3 `rewind` kernel part [draft]:** the derived reset of Part XIV restricted to `above st m`:
  `split(internal, [above])` then `release` of the new authority. Plus an explicit §36 check
  (`AdminRight`: `internal` active and `MetaRight` on the stack value) before the split, like
  `IssueStatic.live/metaRight`. Under the stack invariants (internal a `Modify` authority held by
  the stack value whose footprint contains the cells) and I3, `ok` holds exactly when DS-v1's
  condition and §36 hold; this converse is **not proved** here.
- **R4 "removes m and every mark above it":** "above" = later in the ordered list;
  `marks := takeWhile (· ≠ m)`. Blocks with base `≥ m.top` are forgotten [draft].
- **R5, R6, R7:** moved to DS-R9, DS-R10, DS-R11 above (they change verdicts or arrival states;
  review round 2, DS-1).
- **R8 Library runs:** `DStep.kernel` admits any kernel step of non-administrative code.
# Readings — key `machine` (formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Machine.lean, spec v0 §8–§20)

Format: clause, quote, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict changes. "Representation" = changes no accepted program.

## Spec problems

**S1. §15.3 (bytes "required").** Quote: "the bytes **required** for the representation being read are initialized". §15 ¶5 makes 4, 6, 7 parametric, so 3 should be concrete, but which bytes are "required" depends on the read type's representation, which §10 ¶6 defers ("Constraints on invalid representations, padding bytes, and type alignment will be specified by the corresponding specifications").
Reading used (brief): every byte of the accessed range (`Alloc.InitRange (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len` inside `CanRead`).
Alternative: a type-dependent required-byte set, as a parameter like 4, 6, 7.
Example: raw typed read of a 2-byte representation whose second byte is padding and was never written: `ub` under the reading used, `ok` under the alternative (other conditions holding).

**S2. Byte read vs typed read (§20.2 ¶1, §16 ¶5, §18 ¶1).** Quotes: §20.2 ¶1 "A valid **byte read** does not modify memory state … A raw typed read must **additionally** satisfy type, alignment, and concurrency obligations"; §16 ¶5 "every valid raw byte read of a subrange …"; §18 ¶1 "A data race is UB". No clause lists the conditions of a byte read.
Reading used: one read relation `ReadStep` (typed, with type argument and obligations `ObR`). A byte read is an instance under a context that fixes its obligations. `write_read_sub` and `write_noninterference` quantify over every obligation spec `R` and every type, so they hold whichever way S2 is decided.
Alternative: a separate `ByteRead` relation without §15.4/§15.6/§15.7.
Example: a raw byte read of byte `x` concurrent with an unordered non-atomic write to `x`: `ok` in the machine under the alternative (byte read has no concurrency obligation), UB under §18.

**S3. §16 ¶3 presupposes a counter (minor).** Quote: "allocation identity and the allocation counter are unaffected", against §9 ¶7 "A monotonically increasing counter is one possible representation, not a language requirement" and §9 ¶12. Formalized with the counter (`WriteStep_frame`: `s'.next = s.next`). Does not block.

## Reading decisions

**R1. Totality form (§20.1 ¶3).** Quote: "Memory-machine relations may be deterministic and mathematically total even when certain obligations are not constructively decidable. A classical proof of totality is not a runtime requirement." The axiom policy of this pass excludes `Classical.choice`, and `∃ o, ReadStep … o` on every state is equivalent to excluded middle on `stat` (resp. `C`, `AllocPre`).
Used: `ReadStep_total` … `AllocStep_total` state `¬¬ ∃ o, …` on every state (constructive, classically equivalent to `∃`), and `*_total_on` state `∃ o` on the interpreter domain (stat proof given, `DecidableRel C`, `WF s`).
Alternative: `∃ o` on every state via `Classical.em` (one line each, axiom `Classical.choice`). Statement form only; no verdict changes.

**R2. Read/write type (§15.4, §15.6, §16.4, §16.5, §20.3 ¶3).** Representation: opaque `Ty : Type`; `ReadStep ObR ac t s o`, `WriteStep ObW ac t w s o`, `Op.read ac t`, `Op.write ac t w`; obligations `dec`/`stat : State → Access → Ty → …`. No structure assumed on `Ty`. (Draft had no type: a `u32` read and a `[u8;4]` read at the same odd address could not get different outcomes.)

**R3. Resolution (§11 ¶2).** Quote: "a means of access produces a place **only if** provenance identifies a registered allocation (live or dead) and the address range is spatially contained within it". Used: `Access.toPlace` defined exactly when registered ∧ `Spatial` ("iff"). Alternative: a resolution defined on fewer accesses. No relation uses `toPlace`, so no verdict changes (representation).

**R4. Freshness and identity assignment (§9 ¶7, §9 ¶11, §13 ¶1).** Representation: counter `next`, `WF s := ∀ i ≥ next, unregistered`; the machine assigns `s.next`; the "fresh identity" precondition of §9 ¶11 is `s.allocs s.next = none` (dead allocations stay registered, so unregistered = never assigned). Alternative: client-supplied identity with a "never assigned" precondition. No verdict changes on admissible states (`WF` makes the precondition true). Outside the domain `AllocStep` may be `ok` on a non-`WF` state, as §9 ¶10 allows.

**R5. "Absence of an intervening write or invalidation" (§16 ¶5).** Used (`Op.KeepsAlloc`): every intervening operation is a read, a creation, a deallocation of another identity, or a write through another provenance. Alternative: no intervening write at all. The hypothesis used is weaker, so `write_read_sub` is stronger; no verdict changes. `ops = []` gives the immediately following read.

**R6. Non-interference ranges (§16 ¶5).** Quote: "nor that of a range disjoint from the written range". Used: absolute half-open address ranges `[ac.addr, ac.addr + ac.len)` and `[ac'.addr, ac'.addr + ac'.len)` disjoint (`RangeDisjoint`, §9 ¶3); "result of a valid read" compared for `ok` reads before and after with the same obligations and type. The theorem also proves `CanRead s' ac' ↔ CanRead s ac'`.

**R7. Deallocation designation (§17).** Representation: by identity `id` (the provenance of the presenting access) plus presented authority `auth : Nat`; recorded token `freeAuth : Option Nat`; compatibility `C : Nat → Nat → Prop` a context parameter with no decision instance in the relation. §17 states no "address = base" condition.

**R8. Interpreter domains (brief: "static obligations and the admissible-state hypothesis as proof arguments"; obligation 1: "static obligations and WF").** Used: `read`/`write` take the `stat` proof; `alloc` takes `WF s` only (what `AllocPreDec ↔ AllocPre` needs); `dealloc` takes `[DecidableRel C]` and no proof. Agreement is proved on these domains, which contain the admissible states. Alternative: `Admissible s` on every interpreter (smaller domain). No verdict changes.

**R9. Executions (§9 ¶9, §20.1 ¶2 b3, §20.3 ¶3).** Representation: `Exec C ObR ObW ops s₀ s`, a list of `ok` steps under one context; a read step leaves the state unchanged; a `ub` step supplies no state and never occurs inside an execution. `Reachable s₀ s := ∃ ops, Exec … ops s₀ s`; admissibility of `s₀` is a hypothesis of the theorems (`Exec.admissible`), not part of `Reachable`.

**R10. Restrictive derivation subrange (§14 ¶1 b2).** Used: `ac.addr ≤ ac'.addr ∧ ac'.addr + ac'.len ≤ ac.addr + ac.len` (same arithmetic as §15 ¶1). A zero-length derivative at the source's end address counts as a subrange. Alternative: require `ac'.addr < ac.addr + ac.len` for zero length. `Derive` is used by no relation (formation has no transition, §14 ¶4), so no machine verdict changes.

**R11. Written representation.** Representation: `w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat`, only positions `[0, len)` used; a list would add a length-mismatch case that no clause classifies.

**R12. Citation numbering.** Paragraphs counted with a list belonging to the paragraph that introduces it. The frame clause "Bytes in other allocations …" is cited §16 ¶3 (the brief writes §16 ¶4, which under this count is "Conditions 4, 5, and 6 …").

## Design note (formal/DESIGN.md, not decided here)

DESIGN.md "Representation": "Semantics is a step function where the spec is deterministic". Spec §20.1 ¶1: "Raw memory-model operations are interpreted by **transition relations**", and a total step function would need a classical decision of `stat`. The module follows the spec (relations + computable interpreters + agreement). DESIGN.md also asks for fuel interpreters over sequences; none is provided here (not in the brief).

# Report — corpus-kernel (brief obligation 7, kernel and arena part)

Files (new, untracked, nothing committed, no other file touched):
- `formal/Ern/Corpus/Runner.lean` (module `Ern.Corpus.Runner`, 406 lines, imports `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena`)
- `formal/Ern/Corpus/MM3H.lean` (module `Ern.Corpus.MM3H`, ~907 lines, imports `Ern.Corpus.Runner`)
Both are test modules; no model module imports them.

## Status

- `lake build Ern.Corpus.Runner Ern.Corpus.MM3H`: success; `lake env lean` on both files prints nothing (no warning).
- `axcheck.sh Ern.Corpus.Runner Ern.Corpus.MM3H`: Runner 244 constants / 94 theorems, MM3H 160 / 51, list outside propext/Quot.sound `#[]` (no `Classical.choice`).
- No `sorry/admit/native_decide/axiom/noncomputable/set_option`; no Mathlib tactic; no line over 100 characters; every `def/theorem/abbrev/structure/inductive/instance` has a docstring citing a § clause (script-checked); no draft citation (no MM-0x, pass, O4.x labels; "material" = `ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`, non-normative, cited as the source of expected verdicts as the brief requires).
- Whole build: all 49 case `decide` proofs take ~11 s for the module.

## Runner (Ern.Corpus.Runner)

Definitions: `KD`/`KD.toK` (test contract from lists: SharedMutable, Pinned, ExternalDone, Deallocable, FreeCompat pairs; DeclaredDisjoint False; Satisfiable True) with decidability instances; `Op` (19 constructors: O1–O16 with the reference argument forms — `derive` takes a region, `enter`/`alloc` take a `LocalShape` — plus `newArena st i`, `issue i region dst`, `reset i`); `Verdict`, `verdictOf`; `KRel R A` (kernel relation read on library outcomes, registry unchanged on `ok`); `OpRel k L o` (kernel `XStep` relations for O1–O16; `NewArenaStep [] st i L`, `IssueD k i r d L`, `ResetD i L` for the arena ops); `kg`, `lstep k L o : Outcome3 LState` (computable; issue follows `IssueD`: static, availability `fail`, `SplitPre`, `StorePre`; reset follows `ResetD`: `DerivePre`, `ReleasePre`, `ResetNoDeps`); `next`; `lrun`; `final`; `RunsTo k st os L` (fields `run : lrun … = some L`, `lreach : LReach k st L`, `reach : Reachable k st L.kern`); `Runs k st os := RunsTo k st os (final k st os)`.

Theorems:
| Theorem | Statement | Clauses |
|---|---|---|
| `KD.ddSound` | `DDSound d.toK` | §61, §80 |
| `kg_sound` | `KRel (Guarded p s) L.arenas (kg L p s)` | §58 |
| `lstep_sound` | `OpRel k L o (lstep k L o)` for every op, all three outcomes | §58, §60–§78 |
| `opRel_ok` | `OpRel k L o (.ok L') → LStep k L L'` | Part XIV, §57 |
| `lstep_ok` | `lstep k L o = .ok L' → LStep k L L'` | Part XIV, §58 |
| `lrun_reach` | `LReach k st L → lrun k L os = some L' → LReach k st L'` | Part XIV, §46 |
| `runsTo` | `(lrun k (LState.init st) os).isSome = true → Runs k st os` (so `LReach` and `Reachable` of the final state) | §47, §57, Part XIV |
| `rejects` / `fails` / `oks` | computed verdict `reject`/`fail`/`ok` ⇒ `OpRel k L o .reject` / `.fail` / `.ok (next k L o)` | §58 |

Reading/representation choices of the runner (each changes no accepted program):
- `newArena` passes `others = []` to the §56 guard: library states of these runs hold arenas only. A later wave with pools must add the other registries (the `Op` and `OpRel` of `newArena` would take them).
- `final` falls back to `LState.init` on a failed run; it is only used under `runsTo`'s hypothesis, and every case states `RunsTo` (whose `run` field says the run is all `ok` and ends at the named state).
- No `LRun` soundness (only `LReach`/`Reachable`, which the brief asks for).

## Cases (Ern.Corpus.MM3H)

Twin = positive twin (material §0 rule 2). Verdicts on the step under test are stated with the operation's relation on the reached state and decided by `decide` (`IssueD`/`ResetD`/`NewArenaStep` via `rejects`/`fails` of the runner). Every reached state is given by `RunsTo` (all steps `ok`, `LReach`, `Reachable`).

| id (theorem) | source summary | expected (source) | obtained | class | twin | mismatch cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H01 | Modify param on whole, then Observe on a part of the same local | reject (mat. A) | reject (`DeriveStep`, §43.3, §60.2) | N3 | without 1st param: derive ok; call with 1st param alone ok | — |
| H02 | Observe whole then Modify part | reject | reject (§43.4, §60.2) | N3 | without observation: ok | — |
| H03 | Y holds stored Modify on part p of X; write p via root of X | reject | reject (`Write3Step`, §43.3, §67.1) | N3 | without stored authority: ok | — |
| H04 | swap by split / by two derive Modify | ok / reject | ok / reject (§61, §60.2, §85) | N3 | derive of the other element: ok | — |
| H05 | transfer(x, x.f) ; twin x.f→tmp, tmp→x.f | reject / ok | reject (§63.2, §63.3) / ok | N3 | yes (the material's) | — |
| H06 | derive M, derive O below, release both, write via root | ok | ok | N3 | — | — |
| H07 | callee stores into a static a value anchored on a caller local | reject at transfer | reject (§63.6 AnchorOrder) | N3 | without anchor: ok | — |
| H08 | return anchored on derivative of derivative of a param | ok | ok (transfer, exit) | N3 | — | — |
| H09 | return anchored on callee local via two derivations | reject | reject (§63.6) | N3 | without anchor: ok | — |
| H10 | part holding access derived from container anchor A transferred, container ended, end of A | reject at end of A | reject (`ReleaseStep`, §62.3) | N3 | without the transfer: endUse, release ok | — |

## LibRunner (Ern.Corpus.LibRunner)

### Definitions
- `CState ⟨kern, arenas, pools, nId, res, stacks, fresh⟩` holds one kernel state shared by the arena registry, the pool registry with its fresh identity counter and ghost resolutions, and the stack registry with its fresh mark counter. It has projections `toL : LState`, `toP : PState` and `toD : DState`, the setters `setL`, `setP` and `setD`, and `CState.init` (§47).
- Guard parameters for §56:
  - `othersA = [HandlePool.liveInternals, DataStack.stackInternals]`
  - `othersP = [Arena.liveInternals, stackInternals]`
  - `othersD = [Arena.liveInternals, HandlePool.liveInternals]`

  - O1–O16, `issue` and `reset` use `Ern.Corpus.OpRel` on `C.toL`. For a kernel op this is the kernel relation on `C.kern` with the arenas unchanged.
  - `newArena` uses `NewArenaStep C.othersA`.
  - Pool operations use `NewPoolStep C.othersP`, `AllocSlotStep`, `ResolveStep`, `ResolveManyStep`, `UnresolveStep` and `FreeSlotStep` on `C.toP`.
  - Stack operations use `NewStackStep C.othersD`, `PushStep`, `MarkStep`, `RewindStep` and `GrowStep` on `C.toD`.
- `cstep k C o` is computable. For kernel and arena ops it is `Ern.Corpus.lstep` on `C.toL`, lifted. It has explicit executors `allocSlotOut`, `resolveOut`, `resolveManyOut`, `unresolveOut`, `freeSlotOut`, `pushOut`, `markOut`, `rewindOut` and `growOut`. `allocSlot` picks the lowest free slot (`firstFree`), which is one of the outcomes the relation allows.

|---|---|---|

| `cstep_sound` | `CRel k C o (cstep k C o)` for every `o` | §58, §60–§78, annex, DS-v1 |
| `crejects` / `cfails` / `coks` | computed `reject` / `fail` / `ok` ⇒ the corresponding outcome of `CRel` (`ok` to `cnext`) | §58 |
| `LStep.kseq` | arena library step ⇒ `KSeq` of kernel steps | Part XIV, §57 |
| `crel_kside` | `ok` step with the `kok` check ⇒ `KSeq` of kernel steps, or (`freeSlot` only) `ContentEndPre ∧ kern' = endUseEff kern q` | §57, §67, §69; D.2, D.3; DS-v1 |
| `crun_reach`, `crunsTo` | a completed run from `CState.init` ⇒ `CReach` and `HandlePool.XReach` (kernel steps + ends of slot contents) | §47, §57 |
| `crun_reachable`, `CRunsTo.reachable` | a completed run with no `freeSlot` ⇒ kernel `Reachable` | §57 |

- Arena ops (`issue` = `split` + `store`; `reset` = `derive` + `release`; `newArena` none), stack ops (`push` = split+store, `rewind` = split+release, `grow` = release+split+store, `newStack`/`mark` none) and pool ops other than `freeSlot` are kernel-step sequences:

  - `unresolve` = `release`s
  - `newPool` = none

File edited: `formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean` only. `Ern/Corpus/Lib.lean` and `Ern/Corpus/LibRunner.lean`
were not touched, because nothing in them referred to the renamed names. The pool operations

ghost invariants `PoolWF`, `NoStale` and `CompExcl` and every proof except the renamings below.

- There is no sorry, admit, native_decide, axiom, noncomputable or set_option in the file.

## HP-1 (major): the literal guarantees are stated and refuted, and the proved versions are renamed as same-pool restrictions

Spec passages (contract, HandlePool v0.4 annex = Annex D of `ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`):
- D.4 (3): "`freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné".
- D.3: "aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres. En particulier, aucune
  descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée".
- D.2: "Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du
  pool".
- Brief obligation 5: "transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active
  companion descendant".

### Literal statements (new definitions)

- `FreeGuarantee` (HandlePool.lean:1445) is D.4 (3) as written. Its quantifier ranges over every ghost
  companion `r ∈ L.res`, with no `r.pool = pl.id`, and over every active **strict** descendant `x`
  (`r.comp ∈ ancs x`). Strict is the weaker reading of "descendante". The refutation uses a strict
  descendant, so it also refutes the reading that includes the companion itself.
- `PoolInv` (:1465) is `EntriesDisjoint ∧ NoStale ∧ FreeGuarantee`, as D.4 and the brief state it.
- `ModifyExclusive` (:1541) is D.2 as written. Take an active `Modify` companion `r₁` of a pool `pl`. Any
  active companion `r₂`, of any pool, whose footprint meets a leaf of `pl.storage` must be `r₁`. The
  refutation's second companion covers the **whole** storage (`afp 9 = footprint storage`). It is
  created by a `resolve` that is accepted while the `Modify` companion is already active. So the
  statement is refuted under every reading: "meets a leaf" or "covers all of the storage", state form or
  transition form ("bloque les nouvelles compagnes").

### Refutations (namespace `Witness`, new nested-pool run `nst`, `n0`–`n10`, contract `K0`)

The run is the reviewer's x10, with the states renamed. Pool 0 has storage 0 and `internal` 5. It is
resolved in `Modify` (companion 6, entry 7), and entry 7 is then released by a kernel `release`. A
kernel `derive(6, [1, 2], Modify)` gives authority 8, which is stored in place 4. `newPool(0, 8)` creates
pool 1 over the same storage, and `allocSlot(1, 6)` follows. `n10_reach : PReachI K0 nst n10` is proved,
and every step starts from a `KInv` state, decided through `Arena.KInvB`.

- `Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false` (:2156) proves
  `PReachI K0 nst n10 ∧ KInv n10.kern ∧ ¬ FreeGuarantee K0 n10 ∧ n10.pools[1]? = some plB10 ∧
  Exempt n10.kern plB10.internal 6`. `freeSlot(⟨1,0,0⟩)` of pool 1 is accepted on place 1, while
  companion 6 of pool 0 and its active descendant 8 cover place 1.
- `Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false` (:2168) proves `PReachI K0 nst n10 ∧ ¬ PoolInv K0 n10`.
- `Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false` (:2177) proves that the `Modify` companion 6 of pool 0
  is recorded and active in `n10`. `resolve(1, ⟨1,0,0⟩, Modify)` from `n10` is accepted. The reached
  state is `PReachI`, satisfies `¬ ModifyExclusive`, and has `afp 9 = footprint storage`.

### Proved versions, renamed as same-pool restrictions

The statements and proofs are unchanged. Each docstring now says that it states the same-pool
restriction, not the contract's statement, and points to the refutation.
- `FreeGuarantee` is now `FreeGuaranteeSamePool` (:1455). The docstring notes that it is weaker
  (same pool only) and stronger (it also covers the companion itself).
- `PoolInv` → `PoolInvSamePool` (:1471).
- `freeGuarantee_of` → `freeGuaranteeSamePool_of` (:1487).
- `pool_inv_preserved` → `pool_inv_preserved_same_pool` (:1510).
- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc` → `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool` (:1531).
- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` → `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool` (:1552).
- The `CompExcl` docstring (:966) now says that it is the same-pool restriction of the D.2 sentence.
- `pool_entries_disjoint` and `pool_no_stale_access` keep their names and statements, which are D.4 items
  1 and 2 as written. Only their proof term now cites `pool_inv_preserved_same_pool`.

No other module used the old names. `grep` over `formal/` found none.

### Contract defect (record)

D.3 contradicts itself, and D.3's precondition contradicts D.4 (3), on nested pools. D.3 exempts
"`internal` et ses ancêtres". When the `internal` of pool B is derived from a companion of pool A, that
companion is an ancestor of B's `internal`. It is therefore exempt for `freeSlot` on B. The model
follows the precondition (`ContentEndPre`, `Exempt`), as the task requires. So `freeSlot` succeeds while
an active descendant of a companion covers the slot. That descendant is B's `internal` itself, and it
is active and covers the slot. This contradicts D.3 "En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une
compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée", D.4 (3), and the brief's transition guarantee.

D.2's sentence fails for the same reason. B's companion descends from A's `Modify` companion, so the
kernel accepts its derivation, and a new `Modify` companion is created over A's whole storage.

Two readings of the D.2 sentence exist. If "nouvelles compagnes" means only new companions of the
same pool, then `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool` is the statement. Under the wording as
written, which `ModifyExclusive` formalizes, the sentence is false. This needs arbitration. Brief
obligation 5 ("PoolInv = … + transition guarantee", theorem `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`) therefore
cannot be discharged as stated. It is a contract (specification-side) defect, not a module defect.

Possible repairs, which are not chosen here:
- (a) restrict the exemption to `internal` and the ancestors that are not companions of a live
  pool or their descendants;
- (b) restrict D.4 (3) and D.2 to the slot's pool;
- (c) forbid `newPool` with an `internal` that descends from a live companion.

Each of these changes accepted programs. For example, (a) and (c) reject the `freeSlot` or the
`newPool` of `n10`.

## HP-3 (minor, record only, no code change)

When a pool is dead (its `internal` is inactive, for example after a kernel `release` of `internal`),
its registry entry is kept. `HandleOK` still holds for its handles, and `ResolveRight` (which contains
`Active internal`) is checked first. So `resolve` on that pool gives `reject`, and `reject` is the only
outcome. The reviewer's evidence is `DeadPool.dead_pool_rejects` in `review2/libs/misc.lean`.

§89 says "a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure", and by §58 defined failure is
`fail`. D.1 says "détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle". No
recorded reading covers this case. H-R3 orders the right before handle validity, H-R3's alternative
gives the same verdict here, and H-R4 covers only a missing index. `pool_resolve_stale_fails` cites §89
but assumes `ResolveRight`, which excludes this case. This is recorded as a reading gap that needs
arbitration:
- (a) keep `reject`;
- (b) treat a dead pool's handle as a stale identity, which gives `fail`.

The example whose verdict changes is `resolve(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩, Observe)` on `wd` (`w4` after `release(3)`):
(a) gives `reject` and (b) gives `fail`. Nothing changed in code.

## HP-4 (minor, record only, no code change)

`freeSlot` is a transition outside O1–O16 (`XStep.contentEnd`). On a `PReachI` state whose slot content
is `Init`, `freeSlot` ends that content. Kernel `endUse` is rejected both for the slot place and for the
storage root, and `internal` stays active. The reviewer's evidence is
`FreeNotKernel.free_outside_kernel` in `review2/libs/misc.lean`. The library run's kernel side
therefore leaves kernel `Reachable`.

This conflicts with §36 ("These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel") and §89
("do not modify the authority-discipline kernel"). Yet the behaviour is prescribed by D.3 (the exemption
of `internal` and its ancestors in the end-of-use checks) and by brief obligation 5 ("freeSlot ends the
entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors"). This is a
**brief/contract-versus-spec contradiction** (§36 and §89 against D.3 and obligation 5). It is recorded,
not resolved: the task forbids changing the pool operations, and the charter hierarchy says such
contradictions are reported. The existing `Witness.freeSlot_not_endUse` (on `w4`) shows only an
`Uninit` slot. The `Init` case is the reviewer's `free_outside_kernel`, which was not imported into the
module.

## Not done

- The nested-pool case was not added to the corpus (`Corpus/Lib.lean`) because the corpus encodes
  cases from their sources with expected verdicts, and this case has no source verdict. The witness
  lives in `HandlePool.Witness`, next to the other contract-problem witnesses.
- `readings/handlepool.md` and `reports/handlepool.md` were not edited, because they are outside the
  allowed files. Their entries on `pool_inv_preserved`, `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc` and
  `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` now refer to the `_same_pool` names. The contract defect above should
  be added to the readings as a new entry that needs arbitration.
# Fix round 1: kernel (KM-1, KM-2)

Branch `reference/memory-model-v0`. Nothing is committed. The full project builds with
`lake build` in `formal/` and prints no warnings. The forbidden-token grep prints nothing.
`axcheck.sh` prints empty lists for every touched module: Access.Lemmas, Access.Main,
Preserve.{Alloc, DeriveSplitRelease, EndFree, Frames, Small, Transfer} and Lib.HandlePool.

## KM-2: KAux removed from the per-step obligation (fixed)

The defect: `KAux = RootHeldConv` is not a clause of §49 or §57. It was a hypothesis of every
per-operation `*_preserves`, of `op_preserves`/`kstep_preserves` and of `exitFrame_no_dangling`.

### New lemma

`Lemmas.lean`: `rootHeldConv_active` (§49.4, §49.7, §50, §54). It derives the active, origin-less
fragment of `RootHeldConv` from `WF3 ∧ I1 ∧ NoDangling`. It is the reviewer's `conv_active`
(review2/main-preserve/kaux2.lean).

The proofs applied `RootHeldConv` only to an active authority with no origin.

| Theorem | Before | After |

- `op_preserves`: `DDSound k → KInv s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → op ≠ transfer → KInv s'`. This is

- `op_preserves_kAux` (new): `KInv s → KAux s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → KAux s'`, for every

# Report: kernel-main (Access/Main.lean, brief obligation 2)

File: `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Main.lean` (module `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main`, 828 lines). It
imports the six Preserve modules and is new and untracked. Nothing was committed, and no other file
was touched.

## Status

- `lake build Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main` succeeds, and so does the full `lake build` (22 jobs,
  including the other agents' current files). `lake env lean` on the file prints nothing, so there
  are no warnings.
- `axcheck.sh Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main` reports 193 constants and 102 theorems. The list outside
  propext and Quot.sound is `#[]`, so there is no Classical.choice.
- The AGENTS.md grep over the whole tree prints nothing. There is no `noncomputable` and no
  `set_option`.
- All 40 declarations have an English docstring that cites a § clause, checked by script. So do the
  constructors of `KernelOp`, `KStar` and `ReachableDU`. There are no draft citations, and no line is
  longer than 100 characters.
- Spec passages read in full before coding: §39, §44, §45, §47, §54, §57, §58, §59, §60–§63, §80.

## Theorems (namespace `Ern.MemoryModel.Access`)

### (e) Operations, steps, reachability, §58, §39

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `KernelOp` (inductive) | the 16 operations O1–O16 with their arguments | §60–§75 |
| `KernelOp.Step k op` (def) | the step relation of the operation, `S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop` | §58, §60–§75 |
| `kstep_iff` | `KStep k s s' ↔ ∃ op, op.Step k s (.ok s')` | §57, §58 |
| `KStar k s` (inductive) | reflexive-transitive closure of `KStep` from `s` | §57 |
| `reachable_iff` | `Reachable k statics s ↔ KStar k (S3.init statics) s` | §57 |
| `op_fail_only_alloc` | `op.Step k s .fail → ∃ pr ow ls, op = .alloc pr ow ls` | §58 |
| `kstep_base` | `KStep k s s' → s'.F.getLast? = s.F.getLast?` | §39 |
| `reachable_base` | `Reachable k statics s → s.F.getLast? = some 0`, on every reachable state with no invariant needed | §39, §47 |
| `reachable_base_mem` | `Reachable k statics s → 0 ∈ s.F` | §39 |

### (a) Preservation

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `op_preserves` | `DDSound k → KInv s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → (∀ src dst, op ≠ .transfer src dst) → KInv s'` | §57, §58, §60–§75 |
| `op_preserves_kAux` | `KInv s → KAux s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → KAux s'` for **all 16** operations, transfer included (auxiliary) | §40, §49.7 |
| `kstep_preserves` | over `KStep`: `DDSound k → KInv s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∨ ∃ src dst, TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s')` | §57, §58 |
| `kstep_preserves_kAux` | `KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KAux s'` (auxiliary) | §40, §49.7 |
| `op_preserves_heldAnchored` | `WF3 s → HeldAnchored s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → HeldAnchored s'` for **all 16** operations, transfer included | §44, §65, §63, §73 |
| `kstep_preserves_heldAnchored` | the same over `KStep` | §44, §57 |
| `transfer_dst_usable_of_noDangling` | `WF3 s → TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → NoDangling s' → s'.Usable dst` | §63.1, §54 |
| `transfer_kinv_iff` | `KInv s → HeldAnchored s → TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → (KInv s' ↔ s'.Usable dst)` | §57, §63 |
| `op_preserves_of_dst_usable` | `DDSound k → KInv s → HeldAnchored s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → (∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst) → KInv s' ∧ HeldAnchored s'` | §57, §63 |

(Restated in fix round 1, finding KM-2: no statement of this section takes `KAux` except the two
`_kAux` theorems; see `fix1-kernel.md`.)

The strongest true transfer statement is `transfer_kinv_iff`. On states with `KInv ∧
HeldAnchored`, "destination usable after" is sufficient (the Transfer module's theorem). It is also

authority of the current frame over the destination stays active and still covers the destination's

Private helpers: `heldAnchored_of_step` (the shared argument: §49.8 gives a usable holder before
the step), `getElem?_append_cases`, `initP_len`, `initP_get`, `initP_get'`, `initA_get`,
`rootIdx_get`, `statics_parent`, `statics_owner`, `init_usable`, `init_lt_of_mem_footprint`,
`init_rootPlace`, `init_root_inj`. Reused from other modules: `Frames.getElem?_inj_of_lt`,
`Frames.range_pairwise_lt`, `Frames.exists_getElem?_of_mem`, `EndFree.endUse_active`,
`EndFree.free_active`, and `Alloc.guarded_ne_fail`. No forbidden list lemma is used.

## HeldAnchored: the conjecture holds

`HeldAnchored` holds at `S3.init`, since there is no derived authority. It is preserved by every
kernel step from a `WF3` state (`op_preserves_heldAnchored`). No counterexample exists for any
operation:

- **derive, split, enterFrame, alloc:** new authorities are frame-held or have no origin.
  `enterFrame` parameters become frame-held.
- **release:** filters only the released anchor.
- **depend:** only adds anchors.
- **store:** anchors the stored authority (§65 effect).
- **transfer:** the Transfer module's theorem.
- **exitFrame:** a surviving anchor maps to itself (`firstSurv (x :: ancs x) = x`).
- **endUse:** an authority that stays active is not held within `p`, so its holder's `D` is kept.
- **free:** keeps `D`.
- **read, write, writeShared, pin, unpin:** keep `A` and `D`.

So P-T2 (Transfer report) cannot occur on `ReachableDU` states. Its counterexample `ahx` is not
reachable by such runs.

## Obligations not proved

Two items of brief obligation 2 are **not proved in the brief's form**, because they are false
under v0 (spec defect P-M1 = SP-A1, §57/§63; counterexample `transfer_breaks_kinv`):

1. "Preservation of `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan` by every step": proved for every
   operation **except `transfer`** (`op_preserves`, `KInv s → step ok → KInv s'`, no auxiliary
   hypothesis). For `transfer` it fails (`transfer_breaks_kinv`); only the conditional
   `transfer_kinv_iff` (under the auxiliary `HeldAnchored`) is proved, and `kstep_preserves` is a
   disjunction.
2. "Reachable invariant from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound`": refuted
   (`reachable_kinv_false`). Only the conditional `reachableDU_kinv` (runs whose transfers keep
   the destination usable, plus `StaticsOK`) is proved.

Both are blocking for the PR under the brief's rule. Also open, and nothing needs it: whether
`HeldAnchored` holds on **every** `Reachable` state. The preservation proof uses `WF3` before the step, and `WF3` fails after the
ownership-cycle transfer.

## Readings (representation only)

1. **"Every step except transfer" over unlabelled `KStep`** is stated as a disjunction
   (`kstep_preserves`: preserved, or the step is an accepted transfer). Over the labelled
   operations it is `op ≠ .transfer` (`op_preserves`). A hypothesis such as "not a transfer step"
   on `KStep` would exclude pairs `(s, s')` that both a transfer and another operation produce.
   The disjunction avoids that.
2. **§59 "permitted write"** is keyed on the executed operation, not existentially over the
   operations relating `s` and `s'`. "Including during a derived `issue`" is covered by `store`,
   because `issue` is a library operation. The transfer disjunct is read as the draft reads it: a
   destination leaf with a corresponding source leaf `Init` before the step.
3. **§59 global form (`init_history`).** It is stated over an explicit run (`KStar`) through a
   witness step `t → t'`. It does not assert that the leaf stays `Init` after `t'`, or throughout
   in the declared case. That stronger history form was not requested.
4. **§39 "the base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never
   exits"** is read as: the bottom of the stack is 0 on every reachable state
   (`reachable_base`). It needs no invariant, because only `exitFrame` pops a frame and §73.1
   requires a caller.
5. **§58 "only `alloc` may produce `fail`"** is stated over `KernelOp.Step`. "Leaving the state
   unchanged" holds by representation: `Outcome3.fail` carries no state. This is kernel-defs
   reading 47.
6. **`KAux` and `HeldAnchored`** are auxiliary invariants. Neither is a clause of §57. Since fix
   round 1 only `HeldAnchored` is needed by the `KInv` induction (for `transfer`); `KAux` is
   preserved separately (`op_preserves_kAux`) and kept in the conclusion of `reachableDU_kinv`. Both are discharged on the reachable states of `reachableDU_kinv`, whose
   conclusion contains `KInv` exactly.

## Problems found / for arbitration

- **P-M1 (= SP-A1 / P-T1, now at the level of §57).** §57 is false as stated
  (`reachable_kinv_false`). The witness satisfies both of §57's hypotheses, `DDSound` and
  well-formed statics. The exact repair, on states where the auxiliary invariants hold, is "the
  transfer destination is usable in the resulting state" (`transfer_kinv_iff`). This is the
  draft's dropped clause. Adding it to §63 as a precondition would make `reachableDU_kinv` the
  unconditional §57.
- **P-M2 (P-T2 resolved for these runs).** The §63.7 gap only matters on states without
  `HeldAnchored`. `HeldAnchored` is an invariant along every `KStepDU` run, so with the P-M1 repair
  §63.7 as written suffices.
- **§47 statics (P2, recorded).** `init_kinv` and `reachableDU_kinv` take `StaticsOK` as a
  hypothesis that §47 does not state. Review finding F2 notes that `StaticsOK` (`ShapeOK 0`) also
  requires owners to precede the statics they own. That is stronger than acyclicity, so it narrows
  the domain of the init theorems to declarations listed owner-first.

## F1 (major): `lReach_inv` / `lReachNG_inv` are vacuous conditionals; ArenaInv broken

Spec: §55 item 1, §57, §63 (ok effect), §46 (live).

- New witness, `Arena.lean` namespace `Witness`, subsection "ArenaInv broken by an accepted
  transfer". States `t1`..`t7`, entry `tE`. The run is: alloc place 3 (owner 0), alloc places 4
  and 5 (owner 3), `derive(4,[4],Modify)` = 6, `store(6,5)`, `newArena(4,6)`, `transfer(0,4)`.
  - `arenaInv_broken_by_transfer` proves `LReach K0 st t7` and that `KInv ∧ KAux` holds before the
    transfer. Before the transfer the only entry is `tE` and storage 4 is usable. The
    `TransferStep K0 0 4` is `ok`. After it the entry is still live, `¬ Usable tE.storage` holds,
    and `¬ ArenaInv t7.kern tE` (§55 item 1 fails).
  - `lReach_inv_conclusion_false`: the conclusion of `lReach_inv` fails at `(K0, st)`.
  - `lReach_inv_hyp_false`: the hypothesis `hK` fails at `(K0, st)`. This follows from the two
    theorems above via `lReach_inv`.
- Docstrings of `lReachNG_inv` and `lReach_inv` rewritten. They now say:
  - each theorem is a conditional whose `hK` is part of the §57 claim, which is false as stated
    (`Access.reachable_kinv_false`);
  - both `hK` and the conclusion are false at the witness instance;
  - the unconditional content is in the per-step lemmas, which are kept unchanged (`lInv_kernel`,
    `lInv_newArena`, `lInv_issue`, `lInv_reset`, `lInv_stepNG`).
